In [[mathematics]], '''Cartan's lemma''' refers to a number of results named after either [[Élie Cartan]] or his son [[Henri Cartan]]:
* In [[exterior algebra]]:<ref>*{{cite book | last = Sternberg | first = S. | year = 1983 | title = Lectures on Differential Geometry | url = https://archive.org/details/lecturesondiffer00ster | url-access = limited | edition = 2nd | publisher = Chelsea Publishing Co. | location = New York | isbn = 0-8218-1385-4 | oclc = 43032711 | page=[https://archive.org/details/lecturesondiffer00ster/page/n16 18]}}</ref> Suppose that ''v''<sub>1</sub>, ..., ''v''<sub>''p''</sub> are linearly independent elements of a vector space ''V'' and ''w''<sub>1</sub>, ..., ''w''<sub>''p''</sub> are such that
::<math>v_1\wedge w_1 + \cdots + v_p\wedge w_p = 0</math>
:in &Lambda;''V''.  Then there are scalars ''h''<sub>''ij''</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''h''<sub>''ji''</sub> such that
::<math>w_i = \sum_{j=1}^p h_{ij}v_j.</math>

* In [[Function of several complex variables|several complex variables]]:<ref>{{cite book
 | author = [[Robert C. Gunning]] and [[Hugo Rossi]]
 | title = Analytic Functions of Several Complex Variables
 | publisher = Prentice-Hall
 | year = 1965|pages= 199}}</ref> Let {{nowrap|''a''<sub>1</sub> < ''a''<sub>2</sub> < ''a''<sub>3</sub> < ''a''<sub>4</sub>}} and {{nowrap|''b''<sub>1</sub> < ''b''<sub>2</sub>}} and define rectangles in the complex plane '''C''' by
::<math>\begin{align}
K_1 &= \{ z_1=x_1+iy_1 | a_2 < x_1 < a_3, b_1 < y_1 < b_2\} \\
K_1' &= \{ z_1=x_1+iy_1 | a_1 < x_1 < a_3, b_1 < y_1 < b_2\} \\
K_1'' &= \{ z_1=x_1+iy_1 | a_2 < x_1 < a_4, b_1 < y_1 < b_2\}
\end{align}</math>
:so that <math>K_1 = K_1'\cap K_1''</math>.  Let ''K''<sub>2</sub>, ..., ''K''<sub>''n''</sub> be simply connected domains in '''C''' and let
::<math>\begin{align}
K &= K_1\times K_2\times\cdots \times K_n\\
K' &= K_1'\times K_2\times\cdots \times K_n\\
K'' &= K_1''\times K_2\times\cdots \times K_n
\end{align}</math>
:so that again <math>K = K'\cap K''</math>.  Suppose that ''F''(''z'') is a complex analytic matrix-valued function on a rectangle ''K'' in '''C'''<sup>''n''</sup> such that ''F''(''z'') is an invertible matrix for each ''z'' in ''K''.  Then there exist analytic functions <math>F'</math> in <math>K'</math> and <math>F''</math> in  <math>K''</math> such that
::<math>F(z) = F'(z)F''(z)</math>
:in ''K''.

* In [[potential theory]], a result that estimates the [[Hausdorff measure]] of the set on which a logarithmic [[Newtonian potential]] is small.  See [[Cartan's lemma (potential theory)]].
